A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIS dataset and MIRage framework. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning experiments, benchmark evaluations, generalization tests and case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds reasoning-model experiments, ablations, efficiency measurements and further safety evaluations.

M1.justification: The MIS construction pipeline, safety-CoT label generation and MIRage fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. The construction prompts are substantively identical. New reasoning-formatted baselines and ablation variants are experimental comparisons, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds MOSSBench evaluation on benign queries designed to trigger oversensitivity and text-only AdvBench evaluation with adversarial suffixes. These extend coverage to distinct over-refusal scenarios and purely textual jailbreaks. AdvBench previously served as a source for MIS construction, not this evaluation. Existing benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v3 adds Customized Safety CoT for Qwen2-VL-7B in Table 15 and ECSO for InternVL2.5-8B in Table 16. Appendix C.1 also adapts existing Textual SFT and VLGuard comparators to reasoning-formatted labels. These are targeted extensions to the otherwise retained comparison methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include fine-tuning MiMo-VL-7B-RL with generated reasoning traces prepended to baseline responses, controlled input/label variants, adversarial-suffix testing and latency/throughput measurements on three benchmarks. MOSSBench adds evaluation on 300 benign queries. These substantially expand the evaluation design; the existing training hyperparameters in Table 7 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4 adds MIRage-specific ablations using original questions as text-only inputs and rewriting safety labels to begin with 'I'm sorry.' v3 also adds reasoning-model bottleneck analysis, inference-efficiency analysis and text-only adversarial robustness testing. The earlier unseen-category experiment, taxonomy analyses and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance-testing procedures. The added experiments maintain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Matched earlier benchmark scores are unchanged, but v3 substantially expands reported outcomes. Table 12 reports MIS-hard ASR of 40.39% for text-only MIRage versus 0.20% for full MIRage; Table 17 reports adversarial-suffix ASR of 21.34% for InternVL2.5-8B versus 8.07% after MIRage. Reasoning-model, MOSSBench, latency and additional comparator results are also new. Extra MIRage rows in Table 4 already appeared in v2 Table 10.

T1.justification: The ASR, RSR, HR and RR definitions and equations (1)-(4) are unchanged. Neither version contains additional formal assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and principal conclusion retain the same claims about the safety visual-reasoning gap, MIS as the first multi-image safety dataset, and MIRage improving safety while preserving general capabilities. The reported 0.83% average improvement is unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 retains the central visual-reasoning explanation but adds interpretations concerning reasoning-model behavioral collapse, ECSO's limited safety self-assessment and text-only transfer without catastrophic forgetting. It also claims no inference-latency degradation, although Table 10 does not uniformly support that interpretation. The conclusion adds future directions involving richer reasoning labels and reinforcement learning.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the new safety-prompt wording, reasoning-label adaptation and latency-measurement frameworks, and states that source code accompanies the supplementary materials. Table 19 reports 3927 MIS training examples alongside the retained approximate 4k description. Conversely, v2's global batch size of 128 and four-hour training statement disappear; hardware and Table 7 remain documented.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to ECSO, MOSSBench, MiMo-VL and Visual Contextual Attack, removes BLIP-2, and adds a training-dataset attribute comparison in Table 19. The central positioning around multi-image safety remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites merge the MIS overview and taxonomy, combine open- and closed-model discussion, reorganize Section 4 and move the baseline enumeration into the appendix. MIRage's separate subsection becomes a paragraph. Conference headers, author-year citations and additional statements are introduced, while most existing prose and the overall narrative remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds eight tables covering the new experiments and training-dataset comparison, expands Table 4 with previously reported MIRage rows, and distinguishes prompt-based rows visually in Table 15. Main tables and several figures are relocated within the ICLR layout. Existing figures and case-study illustrations are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The new ablations and safety-prompt/ECSO comparisons strengthen evidence for the input-and-label explanation, while benign-query and text-only evaluations address useful coverage gaps. These gains are qualified by sparse details for new experiments and unchanged uncertainty reporting. The new no-latency-degradation claim overstates Table 10: MSSBench-Safe per-sample times increase from 3.6 to 4.2 seconds and 2.4 to 2.6 seconds. Losing batch-size and training-time disclosures also slightly weakens reproducibility.
